officialSources.finding: Exact @cloudbase/node-sdk 3.18.7 npm tarball inspected locally; package metadata says MIT, Node >=12, and exact @cloudbase/database 1.4.3 dependency. SHA-256 is recorded in cloudBaseSdkAudit.
Exact @cloudbase/database 1.4.3 npm tarball inspected locally; package metadata says ISC. SHA-256 and relevant source observations are recorded in cloudBaseSdkAudit.
CloudBase database add accepts data and can use a specified document ID; this is API capability evidence, not concurrent idempotency proof.
The Node SDK add example accepts an explicit _id. The master document is not pinned to the locally observed 3.18.7 SDK and does not prove concurrent uniqueness or transaction recovery.
DATABASE_DUPLICATE_WRITE describes a duplicate indexed key, including a duplicate document ID; exact error handling still needs runtime verification.
Document database transactions run server-side through Node SDK; transaction operations include add and have a 10-second maximum.

Node.js 20.19.2 documents createHash, explicit input encoding for Hash.update, and lowercase hexadecimal Hash.digest('hex'); documentation supports the API shape but is not evidence of local execution on the selected runtime.

apiShape: Node SDK declarations expose startTransaction and runTransaction, and CollectionReference.add returns a result shape that may include id, ids, inserted, ok, and requestId.
Database 1.4.3 source returns inserted=1, ok=1, id, and requestId for a successful one-document transaction add; a successful single add returns id and requestId.
sourceObservations: database 1.4.3 collection.add returns a truthy-code result instead of throwing
database 1.4.3 runTransaction awaits callback success before attempting commit

localAdapter.behavior: Accept only a one-document receipt with a nonempty id; reject truthy-code or malformed values using a generic error; transaction mode also requires inserted=1 and ok=1.
